_comment: Luna's Work asset source catalog: which source fits which asset kind (kinds = KINDS of src/lunasworkAssetPipeline.js). Read by src/lunasworkAssetCatalog.js; the Director (casting) and the Critic (judging) use it as a fixed menu. costClass: free = a free library, local = runs on this PC, paid = spends Higgsfield credits. needsKey = an API key in LunaCore's asset key store is needed to import from the source (Higgsfield uses its own CLI login, so it is false there). ComfyUI model families come only from the AMD GPU rule (AMD_GPU_RULE). Higgsfield model ids are UNVERIFIED: only ids already used in this repo are listed (gpt_image_2_6 from the asset tools and their tests; soul, nano-banana, seedream, flux-kontext and image-to-3d from the old credit table of src/lunasworkAssetCost.js). Checked 2026-11-25 on the work PC with higgsfield CLI 1.2.2: `higgsfield model list --json` and `higgsfield model get gpt_image_2_6 --json` both fail with 'Error: No workspace selected.' (exit 4; `higgsfield workspace status` says no workspace selected), so the live list could not be read and nothing was logged in or changed. The higgsfield-generate skill's model-catalog.md confirms gpt_image_2_6 but names the others differently (nano_banana_flash / nano_banana_pro, seedream_v5_pro, text2image_soul_v2 / soul_cinematic, multi_image_to_3d; Flux Kontext Max without an id) and gives no credit prices, so those ids are kept as they were until the CLI can be read. Credits are rough planning estimates per final, not prices, and are the one source of truth for the spend estimate (src/lunasworkAssetCost.js reads them from here).

sources.toonFit: Mostly photoreal scans and PBR textures: usable for shapes and layout, but every asset needs a toon pass (flat colors, cel shader, outlines). HDRIs only light a scene.
Mixed styles from many authors: search for stylized or low-poly downloadable models; photoreal ones need a toon pass.
Low-poly with flat colors: a good fit for a toon / cel-shaded game, usually only a material swap to the toon shader.
PBR textures and HDRIs: realistic surfaces; use them as a base for hand-painted or flattened toon textures, not as they are.
Large SFX and ambience library; style-neutral, a good fit for SFX after normalization.
Photoreal museum scans with dense meshes: needs retopology and a toon pass; best as reference or for rare props.
Mixed styles, many realistic: pick stylized models; the rest need a toon material pass in Blender.
Sound effects library; style-neutral, a good fit for SFX.
Local drafts: prompt for cel-shaded, flat-color, clean-outline styles; image results are drafts, 3D results need cleanup and a toon material.
Modeled to the art direction through the Blender MCP: the best fit, toon shading and outlines are built in from the start.
Paid finals: strong at stylized and anime-like images when the prompt asks for cel shading; 3D results still need a toon material.
